meta.title: The Parable of the Bags of Gold
meta.verseText: His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!'
meta.theme: God's Kingdom grows when you use what He's given you.

questions.text: What kind of short story did Jesus use to teach truths about God's kingdom?
questions.hint: It starts with the letter 'P'.
questions.explanation: A parable is a short story Jesus used to help people understand important truths about God's kingdom.

questions.text: Where did Jesus lead His disciples to share this story?
questions.hint: It's a mount named after a type of tree.
questions.explanation: After entering Jerusalem, Jesus led His disciples to the Mount of Olives and shared the parable there.

questions.text: In which book of the Bible do we find the Parable of the Bags of Gold?
questions.hint: It's the first book of the New Testament.
questions.explanation: The Parable of the Bags of Gold is found in Matthew 25:14-30.

questions.text: The wealthy master in the story was preparing to go on a long journey.
options: True, but only for a day
questions.hint: He gave his servants gold before he left.
questions.explanation: The story tells of a wealthy man preparing for a long journey who gave his servants treasure to care for while he was away.

questions.text: How did the master decide how much treasure to give each servant?
options: Based on what he knew each one could handle
He gave everyone the exact same amount
He gave the most to the youngest
questions.hint: He knew his servants well.
questions.explanation: The master gave different amounts based on what he knew each servant could handle.

questions.text: What did the first two servants do with the gold they were given?
options: They put it to work and it doubled
They hid it in the ground
questions.hint: Their gold multiplied!
questions.explanation: Both servants used what they were given, and their gold doubled.

questions.text: The first two servants waited a long time before deciding to use their gold.
options: False, they got moving right away
True, they waited until it felt safe
False, they returned the gold immediately
questions.hint: The lesson says they didn't hide or wait.
questions.explanation: The first two servants didn't hide the gold or wait until it felt safe; they got moving right away.

questions.text: How did the master feel when he saw what the first two servants had done?
options: He celebrated them and was filled with joy
questions.hint: It was a happy moment.
questions.explanation: The master celebrated both servants and was filled with joy because they used what they were given.

questions.text: What did the third servant do with his bag of gold?
options: He buried it in the ground
He gave it to the poor
questions.hint: He put it in the dark, underground.
questions.explanation: The third servant made a different choice and buried his gift in the dark instead of using it.

questions.text: What did the third servant say kept him from using his gift?
questions.hint: It's an emotion that makes us afraid to try.
questions.explanation: The third servant admitted that fear kept him from trying; he didn't trust his master and hid the gift.

questions.text: The master was upset with the third servant mainly because the servant lost the gold.
options: False, it was because the servant didn't even try
True, the servant spent it all
False, the master was never upset
questions.hint: The gold wasn't lost, just hidden.
questions.explanation: The master was upset because the servant didn't even try; the gift was wasted in hiding, not lost.

questions.text: How many servants in the story were trusted with bags of gold?
questions.hint: Two used it and one buried it.
questions.explanation: All three servants were trusted with gold, but each chose to do something different with it.

questions.text: What did the master say to the faithful servants? 'Well done, good and faithful ______!'
questions.hint: It's what the men were called in the story.
questions.explanation: In Matthew 25:21, the master says, 'Well done, good and faithful servant!'

questions.text: A parable is a short story used to teach an important ______.
questions.hint: Something real and important that we can learn.
questions.explanation: Jesus used parables to help people understand important truths about God's kingdom.

questions.text: What does the gold in the parable represent for us today?
options: The gifts and things God has given us to use
Gold we will find in heaven
questions.hint: Think about talents, abilities, and blessings.
questions.explanation: The gold represents the gifts God gives each of us, which He invites us to use for His kingdom.

questions.text: Who does the master in the parable represent?
questions.hint: He is in heaven now and invites us to use our gifts.
questions.explanation: Jesus, our Master, is in heaven now and invites us to use everything He has given us.

questions.text: Why was the master pleased with the first two servants?
options: Because they used what they were given
Because they kept the gold perfectly safe
Because they never touched the gold
questions.hint: It wasn't about keeping it safe, but about using it.
questions.explanation: The master was filled with joy because the servants used what they were given instead of hiding it.

questions.text: The main point of the parable is that we should keep our gifts hidden and safe.
options: False, we should give them all away
questions.hint: Remember what happened to the servant who hid his gift.
questions.explanation: The parable teaches the opposite: God's kingdom grows when we use what He's given us, not when we hide it.

questions.text: What was the real problem with the third servant's choice?
options: He let fear stop him from even trying
He gave the gold to someone else
questions.hint: It had to do with not trusting his master.
questions.explanation: The third servant let fear and a lack of trust keep him from trying, so his gift was wasted in hiding.

questions.text: What does the Big Lesson say about God's Kingdom? 'God's Kingdom grows when you ______ what He's given you.'
questions.hint: The opposite of what the third servant did.
questions.explanation: The Big Lesson is: God's Kingdom grows when you use what He's given you.

questions.text: The master knew the third servant was capable of using the gift.
options: False, the servant couldn't do it
questions.hint: The master knew what each servant could handle.
questions.explanation: The master knew the servant was capable, which is why he was upset that the gift was wasted in hiding.

questions.text: What can we learn from the way the first two servants acted quickly?
options: We shouldn't wait or be afraid to use our gifts
We should only act when it feels safe
We should wait for someone to make us
questions.hint: They got moving right away instead of hiding.
questions.explanation: The servants got moving right away without hiding the gold, showing us not to let fear or waiting stop us from using our gifts.

questions.text: If you are good at singing, what is one way to 'use what God has given you'?
options: Sing to worship God and encourage others
Keep it a secret from everyone
Only sing when you are alone
Wait until you are grown up
questions.hint: Think about how a gift can bless others.
questions.explanation: Using your gifts means putting them to work now, like singing to worship God and encourage others.

questions.text: A friend is being left out at school. Using the gift of kindness, what could you do?
options: Invite them to play and include them
Wait for a teacher to fix it
Tell them to figure it out alone
questions.hint: Kindness means helping others feel welcome.
questions.explanation: Using the gift of kindness means acting on it, like inviting a lonely friend to join in.

questions.text: What should you do when fear makes you want to hide your gifts instead of using them?
options: Bury the idea and forget it
Wait until you are never afraid
questions.hint: Remember, the third servant's problem was not trusting his master.
questions.explanation: The third servant let fear stop him. We can trust God and try, knowing He helps us use our gifts.

questions.text: Using your gifts to help God's kingdom grow is only for grown-ups, not kids.
questions.hint: Jesus invites everyone to use their gifts.
questions.explanation: God invites every person, including kids, to use every gift He has given to help His kingdom grow.

questions.text: According to the lesson, God will do great ______ things with the gifts you use.
questions.hint: It's the same word used to describe God's rule and reign.
questions.explanation: The lesson says God will do great kingdom things with the gifts He has given you when you choose to use them.

questions.text: You are good at drawing. Which choice best matches the lesson?
options: Make cards to encourage people who are sad or sick
Never show your drawings to anyone
Stop drawing so no one notices
questions.hint: A gift is meant to be used to bless others.
questions.explanation: Using a gift like drawing to encourage others is exactly how God's kingdom grows when we use what He's given us.

questions.text: Which choice is most like the good and faithful servants in the parable?
options: Using your talents right away to serve God and others
Waiting until everything feels perfectly safe
Hiding your abilities so no one asks you to help
Keeping every good thing just for yourself
questions.hint: The faithful servants got moving right away.
questions.explanation: The faithful servants used what they were given right away, and we follow their example by using our talents to serve.

questions.text: What is a good way to remember to use your gifts this week?
options: Ask God to help you use one gift to bless someone
Make a list and never look at it
Wait for someone else to do it first
Decide you have no gifts at all
questions.hint: Prayer and action go together.
questions.explanation: Asking God to help you use a gift to bless someone puts the Big Lesson into action all week long.

questions.text: The master gave the servants the treasure to care for while he was away.
options: True, but he took it all back first
questions.hint: He trusted them with it before his journey.
questions.explanation: Before leaving, the master called his servants and gave them treasure to take care of while he traveled.

questions.text: Where had Jesus recently entered before teaching this parable?
questions.hint: It was the great city, later in the week.
questions.explanation: Later in the week after entering Jerusalem, Jesus led His disciples to the Mount of Olives to share the parable.

questions.text: Doubling the gold means the servants ended up with less than they started.
options: False, they ended up with twice as much
False, they had exactly the same
questions.hint: Double means two times as much.
questions.explanation: When the servants doubled the gold, they had twice as much as they started with because they put it to work.

story.summary: Later in the week after entering Jerusalem, Jesus led His disciples to the Mount of Olives and told a parable. A wealthy master, preparing for a long journey, gave three servants different amounts of gold based on what each could handle. The first two servants got moving right away, put their gold to work, and doubled it. When the master returned, he celebrated them with joy. But the third servant was afraid, so he buried his gift in the ground. The master was upset, not because the gold was lost, but because the servant didn't even try. Jesus taught that He is our Master in heaven, and He invites us to use every gift He has given us. God's Kingdom grows when you use what He's given you.

scenes.title: Setting Up the Story
scenes.description: Jesus led His disciples to the Mount of Olives and began a parable about a wealthy man preparing for a long journey. Before leaving, the master gave his servants different amounts of treasure to care for, based on what each one could handle.

scenes.title: The First Two Servants
scenes.description: The first two servants didn't hide their gold or wait until it felt safe. They got moving right away, put it to work, and their gold doubled. When the master returned, he celebrated them and was filled with joy.

scenes.title: The Third Servant
scenes.description: The third servant made a different choice. Fear kept him from trying, so he buried his gift in the dark ground. When the master returned, he was upset because the servant didn't even try, even though the servant was capable.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up the Story
scenes.description: Jesus explained that all three servants were trusted with gold, but each chose something different. Jesus, our Master in heaven, invites us to use everything He has given us. God's Kingdom grows when you use what He's given you.

scenes.title: Living It Out
scenes.description: The parable calls each of us to action. Instead of letting fear make us hide our gifts, we can trust God and use our talents right away to serve Him and bless others, and He will do great kingdom things through us.
